issues:
[CRITICAL] Graph.cpp — computeList (`for (size_t i = list.size() - 1; i >= 0; i--)`)
Problem: `i` is `size_t` (unsigned). When `i` reaches 0 and decrements, it wraps to `SIZE_MAX` instead of becoming negative, so the loop never terminates and immediately indexes `list[huge_number]`.
Why it matters: Guaranteed out-of-bounds access / crash or infinite loop on every single call to `computeList`, including the trivial case of an empty list (`list.size()-1` underflows before the loop even starts).
Fix: Use a reverse iteration pattern that doesn't rely on unsigned underflow, e.g. `for (size_t i = list.size(); i-- > 0;)` or iterate with `int64_t`.

[CRITICAL] Link.h — class Link
Problem: `Link` has no user-defined constructor and inherits from `Entity`, whose only constructor is `Entity(Workflow*)`. Because `Entity` has no default constructor, the compiler-generated default constructor for `Link` is implicitly deleted.
Why it matters: `Graph::connect` calls `_workflow->manager().create<Link>()` with zero arguments. This cannot compile — there is no way to construct a `Link` without a `Workflow*`.
Fix: Add `Link(Workflow* workflow) : Entity(workflow) {}` and pass `_workflow` at the call site: `_workflow->manager().create<Link>(_workflow)`.

[CRITICAL] Socket.h — Socket<T>::value() (`ml::Vec<T> connectedValue = csocket->value();`)
Problem: `csocket` is typed as `BaseSocket*`. `BaseSocket` declares no `value()` member (virtual or otherwise) — only `Socket<T>` has a templated `value()`. Calling `csocket->value()` on a `BaseSocket*` does not exist.
Why it matters: This will not compile at all. The whole connected-value propagation mechanism (the core feature of the node graph) is broken at the type level.
Fix: Add a pure virtual `virtual std::any valueAny() ...` or similar type-erased accessor on `BaseSocket`, or template/rework the API so `BaseSocket` exposes a common interface for pulling values across differently-typed sockets.

[CRITICAL] Socket.h — Socket<T>::value() const (`_typeError = "";`)
Problem: `value()` is declared `const`, but it assigns to `_typeError`, a non-mutable member of `BaseSocket`.
Why it matters: This is a straight compile error — you cannot mutate a non-mutable member in a const method.
Fix: Mark `_typeError` as `mutable`, or drop the `const` qualifier from `value()`.

[HIGH] Socket.h — Socket<T>::set(const std::vector<Tin>& value)
Problem: The loop `for (auto& v : _value) _set(value, &v);` passes the *entire* `value` vector into `_set`, which expects a single scalar `Tin`, on every iteration — it never indexes into `value` by position.
Why it matters: Either this fails to compile (`tconv::convert<std::vector<Tin>, T>` almost certainly doesn't exist), or if it somehow compiles via some generic conversion, every element of `_value` gets set to the same wrong "value" derived from the whole vector instead of the corresponding element.
Fix: Iterate with an index: `for (size_t i = 0; i < value.size(); i++) _set(value[i], &_value[i]);`

[HIGH] Graph.cpp — executionList (recursive, no cycle/visited tracking)
Problem: `executionList` recurses into every connected input with zero cycle detection and zero deduplication of already-visited nodes.
Why it matters: Any cyclic graph (even accidental) causes unbounded recursion → stack overflow/crash. Even in acyclic diamond-shaped graphs (two nodes sharing a common input), the shared ancestor node is pushed and executed multiple times, corrupting execution order/semantics.
Fix: Track visited nodes in a set and skip revisits; detect cycles explicitly and fail/log rather than recurse infinitely.

[MEDIUM] MathNode.cpp — MathNode::exec() (`sc->set(scv)`)
Problem: `scv` is `ml::Vec<double>`, obtained from `sc->value()`. `Socket::set` has two overloads: one for scalar `Tin`, one for `std::vector<Tin>`. Unless `ml::Vec` literally *is* `std::vector` (unconfirmed), the vector overload won't match and the scalar overload will be selected with `Tin = ml::Vec<double>`.
Why it matters: This either fails to compile (no valid `tconv::convert<ml::Vec<double>, double>`), or silently does the wrong thing depending on `tconv`'s generic behavior.
Fix: Confirm `ml::Vec`'s relationship to `std::vector`; if it's a separate type, add/overload `set` to accept `ml::Vec<Tin>` explicitly and use index-based assignment.

[MEDIUM] Node.h — _createSocket (`_workflow->manager().create<Socket<T>>(_workflow, this, name)`)
Problem: `Socket<T>`'s constructor expects `Handle<Node>`, but `this` is a raw `Node*`. This only compiles if `Handle<T>` has an implicit non-explicit constructor from a raw pointer.
Why it matters: If `Handle`'s pointer constructor is `explicit` (common defensive practice), this fails to compile. Even if it compiles, constructing a `Handle<Node>` from a raw `this` bypasses whatever ownership/refcounting `ObjectsManager` is supposed to guarantee — this node was never registered as "owned" through this handle, likely creating an inconsistent or dangling handle when the manager's real owning handle is destroyed.
Fix: Store/pass the `Handle<Node>` that `ObjectsManager` returned when this `Node` itself was created, rather than wrapping `this` in a new ad-hoc handle.
